web.description_en: This article provides an in-depth analysis of two symbolic link race condition vulnerabilities in Music.app discovered by Jamf Threat Labs. web.title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It
web.description: A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock  lets someone with physical access to a locked Windows computer start programs without signing in. Whoever uses it gets only a limited account, not administrator control of the machine.   The method was posted yesterday by a researcher who uses the handles MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse , and the endpoint-security firm ThreatLocker tested it the same day and found it works.   There is no fix from Microsoft yet, and nothing shows the method has been used in a real attack.   The technique does not work on every machine. web.title: Researcher Demonstrates Database RCE Exploits Affecting PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
web.description: Low-privilege database accounts that cannot read a single application table can still be used to run code on the database server itself, a researcher has shown, by reaching memory-corruption bugs in the engine code behind ordinary SQL.   The exploits, published yesterday, are the researcher's proofs of concept against PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus a separate Oracle chain that needs no login. None has been seen in a real attack.   The work is by Zheng Yu , a researcher at Depthfirst . A database account's SQL permissions control which tables and schemas it can access, the researcher argues, not the memory-unsafe C and C++ code the engine runs to read, plan, and execute a query.   Common grants give an account enough room to reach that code. PostgreSQL's default TEMPORARY privilege, or the right to create temporary tables in MySQL and ClickHouse, allows an account to create objects or send input that triggers a memory bug.
